tldr: The headline layer across 13 country buckets frames the DR Congo Ebola outbreak almost unanimously through a severity-and-mortality lens — 'fastest-spreading,' 'deadliest-yet,' 'cases doubled' — establishing a record-crisis register before any click. A strong secondary stream from wire services, CGTN, India Today, and Malay Mail foregrounds the capacity-failure angle (outbreak 'outpacing' response, WHO 'pleading' for more aid), while Egypt Independent and AP News alone make unpaid wages the headline story, casting response collapse as a labour crisis rather than a resource gap. Africa-focused outlets (AllAfrica, BBC Africa) carry two angles invisible elsewhere: the Uganda-versus-DRC comparison on outbreak control strategies and a misinformation-to-violence link against health workers. Canada's Globe and Mail is the only outlet to break the uniform alarm register with a vaccine-trial clearance headline.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only outlet to frame the story through individual economic precarity — coupling 'unpaid wages' with 'deadly risk' in the headline and centering a named frontline nurse — the sole pre-click framing that charges the response collapse to labour exploitation rather than logistics or funding gaps.

The only outlet in the corpus to headline the misinformation-to-violence causal link, naming misinformation as the direct driver of attacks on health workers — an angle entirely absent from every other bucket's title-layer coverage.

The only outlet to publish a forward-looking positive-register headline (Moderna vaccine trial clearance by Health Canada), introducing a scientific-response counter-narrative absent from every other title in the corpus and invisible to readers not clicking through.

The only outlet to carry both the Uganda early-declaration defence and the 42-day-rule re-examination angle — policy-and-protocol questions entirely absent from non-African headlines, where the story is framed exclusively as a DRC emergency rather than a global surveillance methodology debate.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the DR Congo Ebola outbreak is universally advertised as a historic record — fastest-spreading, deadliest-ever — while a second, more damning frame renders the response as systemically broken: the outbreak 'outpaces' efforts, the WHO 'pleads,' and health workers abandon posts over unpaid wages, shifting the pre-click moral charge from the virus to the institutions tasked with containing it.
